events.title: The Council of Chalcedon opens
events.description: Bishops summoned by Emperor Marcian met at Chalcedon, across the Bosporus from Constantinople. Its definition of Christ as one person in two natures became orthodoxy in the West and Byzantium but split the eastern churches.

events.title: Chinese officials board the Arrow at Canton
events.description: Qing officials boarded the Arrow, a Chinese-owned ship flying a British flag, and arrested its crew on suspicion of piracy. Britain used the incident as grounds for the Second Opium War.

events.title: The Great Chicago Fire breaks out
events.description: Fire broke out in a barn on DeKoven Street and, driven by strong winds, burned for two days across Chicago. About 300 people died and 100,000 lost their homes, but rebuilding made the city a centre of modern architecture.

events.title: Corporal Alvin York captures 132 German soldiers
events.description: In the Argonne Forest, Corporal Alvin York led a small patrol that silenced German machine guns, killing about 25 soldiers and taking 132 prisoners. He received the Medal of Honor and became a national hero.

events.title: Che Guevara is captured in Bolivia
events.description: Bolivian troops, aided by the CIA, wounded and captured Ernesto 'Che' Guevara in the Yuro ravine. He was executed the next day at La Higuera, and his image became an enduring icon of revolution.
